title: Coordinate blowup lowers the branch number
statement:
Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a regular Noetherian affine scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $t_1,\ldots,t_m\in A$, with $m\geq1$, satisfy the following pointwise coordinate condition: at every point $u$ of $U$, those $t_j$ whose germs lie in the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{U,u}$ are distinct members of a regular system of parameters of that local ring. Such a system in a regular local ring of dimension $d$ means $d$ generators of its maximal ideal. Let $D_U=V(\prod_{j=1}^m t_j)$ and $M_U=V(t_1,\ldots,t_m)$ as closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $b:U^+=\operatorname{Bl}_{M_U}(U)	o U$ be the blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Its standard affine charts, indexed by $1\leq i\leq m$, have coordinate rings $A_i=A[t_j/t_i:1\leq j\leq m,\ j
e i]\subseteq A[1/t_i]$. Write $t_i'=t_i$ and $t_j'=t_j/t_i$ for $j
e i$. On this chart the strict transform of $D_U$ [def-nagata-strict-transform] has equation $\prod_{j
e i}t_j'=0$. For every point $y\in\operatorname{Spec}A_i$, the local ring $(A_i)_y$ is regular; the germs of the factors $t_j'$ with $j
e i$ which vanish at $y$ extend to a regular system of parameters of $(A_i)_y$, and all the other factors are units there. Thus the strict-transform equation in this local ring is a unit times a product of distinct members of a regular system of parameters. The strict transform is empty or a normal crossings divisor, meaning a closed subscheme whose ideal is locally generated by one non-zero-divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] and which etale locally has such an equation, and its number of geometric branches at $y$ equals $\#\{j
e i:t_j'\in y\}\leq m-1$. For $m=1$ the empty product is $1$ and the strict transform is empty. After every etale base change [def-weil-etale-morphism] the displayed chart equations remain valid for the base-changed blowup and strict transform, with the local-parameter assertion made in the local ring of each chosen point. No locality of $A$ or $A_i$ is assumed.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9, printed p. 121, and the depth computation in 4.1.8, printed p. 118: local blowup charts and the strict-transform equation.

proof.text: Put $I=(t_1,\ldots,t_m)$. The finite standard chart cover is [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover]. On its $i$-chart use [lem-trf-coordinate-chart-localization-parameters]: $C=A[I/t_i]$ is Noetherian, $IC=(a)$ for $a=t_i$, and $t_j=az_j$. Thus $f=\prod_jt_j=a^mP$ for $P=\prod_{j\ne i}z_j$. That lemma also supplies regularity and distinct parameter positions for all nonunit members of $(a,(z_j)_{j\ne i})$ at every chart point.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 4.2.9, printed p. 121, coordinate-chart computation, and 4.1.8, printed p. 118; localization at each chart point before applying the local computation.

proof.text: By [def-nagata-strict-transform] the required transform is the scheme-theoretic closure of the inverse image away from the center. The preserved immersion is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: its restriction on each of the finitely many affine charts is $\operatorname{Spec}((C/(f))[1/a])\to\operatorname{Spec}C$. By [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open], restriction of this closure to the chart is its scheme-theoretic image there. Apply [lem-trf-parameter-product-closure-kernel] with $e=m$ and the parameters from Step 1: its ideal is exactly $(P)$.

source.place: Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform; morphisms.tex Tag 01R8, lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image, and Tag 081I, lemma-flat-base-change-scheme-theoretic-image; more-algebra.tex Tag 0AG0, lemma-regular-local-UFD; algebra.tex Tag 00HD, lemma-flat. The parameter-product saturation is the explicit UFD consequence used in ILO VIII 4.1.8 and 4.2.9.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-etale-coordinate-divisor-parameters] to the regular Noetherian chart $\operatorname{Spec}C$ and its $m-1$ functions $z_j$, first with the identity morphism. It gives the local unit-times-parameter-product equation, effective Cartier and normal-crossings properties, and exactly one geometric branch per vanishing $z_j$, hence at most $m-1$. For $m=1$ its zero-coordinate case has $P=1$ and empty divisor.

source.place: Tag 07QP, lemma-dimension-etale-extension, and lemma-regular-etale-extension; algebra.tex Tag 00U4, lemma-etale-at-prime, and Tag 00KU, definition-regular-local; ILO VIII 4.1.6 and 4.1.8, printed pp. 118--119, for geometric branch interpretation.

proof.text: Let $v:W\to U$ be etale, hence flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The canonical comparison [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map] is an isomorphism by [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change], giving the pulled-back chart cover and the same ratio sections. On an affine piece $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset W$, $A\to B$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat], and the tensor-base clause of [lem-trf-parameter-product-closure-kernel] identifies the closure kernel of $\operatorname{Spec}(((C\otimes_A B)/(f))[1/a])\to\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_A B)$ with $(P)(C\otimes_A B)$. As in Step 2 this immersion is the restriction to the affine chart of the quasi-compact, quasi-separated immersion defining the strict transform of $D_W=V(v^*f)$ in $\operatorname{Bl}_{M_W}(W)$, so by [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open] that strict transform restricts on the chart to $V(P)$. Hence the base-changed strict transform has the pulled-back displayed equation. The chart projection to $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Apply [lem-trf-etale-coordinate-divisor-parameters] to this projection for all pointwise parameter and branch assertions, including the empty-product case.
